questions.q: A boat covers 35 km downstream in 2 h and covers the same distance upstream in 7 h. Find the speed (in km/h) of the boat in still water.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Downstream Speed (D) = Distance ÷ Time = 35 ÷ 2 = 17.5 km/h

Upstream Speed (U) = Distance ÷ Time = 35 ÷ 7 = 5 km/h

Speed in Still Water = (D + U) ÷ 2

Speed = (17.5 + 5) ÷ 2 = 22.5 ÷ 2 = 11.25 km/h

∴ The correct answer is 11.25 km/h.

Alternate Method

Given:

Distance (d) = 35 km

Time taken downstream (td) = 2 h

Time taken upstream (tᵤ) = 7 h

Formula Used:

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

Downstream speed = u + v

Upstream speed = u − v

(where u = speed of boat in still water and v = speed of stream)



Calculations:

⇒ Downstream speed (u + v) = 35 ÷ 2 = 17.5 km/h ---- (1)

⇒ Upstream speed (u − v) = 35 ÷ 7 = 5 km/h ---- (2)

⇒ Adding equations (1) and (2):

⇒ (u + v) + (u − v) = 17.5 + 5

⇒ 2u = 22.5

⇒ u = 22.5 ÷ 2

⇒ u = 11.25 km/h

∴ The correct answer is 11.25 km/h.

Additional Information

Speed of Stream

The speed of the water current or stream (v) is calculated as: v = (Downstream Speed − Upstream Speed) ÷ 2.

Relative Speed in Boats

When moving downstream, the speeds are added (u+v); when moving upstream, the stream speed is subtracted from the boat speed (u−v).

Ratio of Speeds

If the distance is constant, the ratio of downstream speed to upstream speed is the inverse of the ratio of time taken: D/U = Tᵤ/Td.

questions.q: What is the compound interest on a sum of ₹25,000 after three years at a rate of 12 per cent per annum interest compounded yearly?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For a 3-year period, use the interest ratio method 3 : 3 : 1.

First year interest (I₁): 12% of 25000 = 3000

Second year interest on I₁ (I₂): 12% of 3000 = 360

Third year interest on I₂ (I₃): 12% of 360 = 43.2

Total CI = (3 × 3000) + (3 × 360) + (1 × 43.2) = 9000 + 1080 + 43.2 = 10123.2

∴ The correct answer is ₹10,123.20.

Alternate Method

Given: Principal (P) = ₹25,000, Rate (R) = 12% p.a., Time (n) = 3 years.

Formula: Amount (A) = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ and CI = A − P



⇒ A = 25000 × (1 + 12/100)³

⇒ A = 25000 × (1.12)³

⇒ A = 25000 × 1.404928

⇒ A = 35123.2

⇒ CI = 35123.2 − 25000

⇒ CI = 10123.2

∴ The correct answer is ₹10,123.20.

Additional Information

Successive Percentage Change

Compound interest is a case of successive percentage increase. For 3 years, the effective rate is [3r + (3r²/100) + (r³/10000)]%.

Difference between CI and SI

For 2 years: Diff = P(R/100)². For 3 years: Diff = P(R/100)² × (3 + R/100).

Compounding Frequency

If interest is compounded half-yearly, the rate is halved (R/2) and the time period is doubled (2n).

questions.q: The LCM of x² − 8x + 15 and x² − 5x + 6 is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Factorize the expressions mentally by finding numbers that sum to the middle term and multiply to the last term.

x² − 8x + 15: Numbers are −3 and −5 → (x − 3)(x − 5).

x² − 5x + 6: Numbers are −2 and −3 → (x − 2)(x − 3).

LCM takes all unique factors: (x − 2), (x − 3), and (x − 5).

∴ The correct answer is (x − 2) (x − 3) (x − 5).

Alternate Method

Given expressions:

P(x) = x² − 8x + 15

Q(x) = x² − 5x + 6

Factorizing P(x) by splitting the middle term:

⇒ x² − 3x − 5x + 15

⇒ x(x − 3) − 5(x − 3)

⇒ (x − 3)(x − 5)

Factorizing Q(x) by splitting the middle term:

⇒ x² − 2x − 3x + 6

⇒ x(x − 2) − 3(x − 2)

⇒ (x − 2)(x − 3)

The Least Common Multiple (LCM) is the product of all distinct factors of the polynomials, each raised to the highest power it occurs in any of the polynomials.

⇒ LCM = (x − 2)¹ × (x − 3)¹ × (x − 5)¹

∴ The correct answer is (x − 2) (x − 3) (x − 5).

Additional Information

LCM and HCF of Polynomials

LCM contains all factors at their maximum power, while HCF (Highest Common Factor) contains only common factors at their minimum power.

The Relationship Property

For any two polynomials f(x) and g(x), the product of the polynomials is equal to the product of their HCF and LCM: f(x) × g(x) = HCF(f,g) × LCM(f,g).

Factor Theorem

A polynomial P(x) has a factor (x − a) if and only if P(a) = 0. This can be used to check factors quickly.

questions.q: The cost of 3 kg of rice is ₹180. The cost of 8 kg of rice is equal to that of 5 kg of Pulse. The cost of 15 kg of pulses is equal to that of 2 kg of tea. The cost of 3 kg of tea is equal to that of 6 kg of walnuts. What is the cost (in ₹) of 10 kg of walnuts?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Apply Chain Rule for 1 kg Walnut: (180 ÷ 3) × (8 ÷ 5) × (15 ÷ 2) × (3 ÷ 6)

1 kg Walnut = 60 × 1.6 × 7.5 × 0.5 = 96 × 3.75 = ₹360

For 10 kg Walnut: 360 × 10 = ₹3600

∴ The correct answer is ₹3600.

Alternate Method

Given:

Cost of 3 kg Rice = ₹180

8 kg Rice = 5 kg Pulse

15 kg Pulse = 2 kg Tea

3 kg Tea = 6 kg Walnuts

Formula Used:

Unit Cost = Total Cost ÷ Quantity

Equivalence Cost: QuantityA × PriceA = QuantityB × PriceB



⇒ Cost of 1 kg Rice = 180 ÷ 3 = ₹60

⇒ 5 kg Pulse = 8 kg Rice = 8 × 60 = ₹480

⇒ Cost of 1 kg Pulse = 480 ÷ 5 = ₹96

⇒ 2 kg Tea = 15 kg Pulse = 15 × 96 = ₹1440

⇒ Cost of 1 kg Tea = 1440 ÷ 2 = ₹720

⇒ 6 kg Walnut = 3 kg Tea = 3 × 720 = ₹2160

⇒ Cost of 1 kg Walnut = 2160 ÷ 6 = ₹360

⇒ Cost of 10 kg Walnut = 10 × 360 = ₹3600

∴ The correct answer is ₹3600.

Additional Information

Chain Rule in Proportion

It is a method used to find a relationship between multiple quantities. The formula is: (Item₁/Item₂) × (Item₂/Item₃) × ... × (Itemₙ−₁/Itemₙ).

Unitary Method

To solve such problems, always find the value of a single unit (1 kg) for each commodity before moving to the next level in the hierarchy.

Inverse Proportion

If the quantity increases while the total cost remains constant, the unit price must decrease: Price ∝ 1 ÷ Quantity.

questions.q: What is the ratio of the simple interest earned on a certain amount at the rate of 21% per annum for 8 years to that earned on the same sum at the same rate for 21 years?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Since the Principal (P) and the Rate of Interest (R) are the same for both cases, Simple Interest (SI) is directly proportional to Time (T).

SI ∝ T (when P and R are constant)

Ratio of Interest = Ratio of Time = T₁ : T₂

Ratio = 8 : 21

∴ The correct answer is 8 : 21.

Alternate Method

Given:

Principal (P₁) = Principal (P₂) = P

Rate (R₁) = Rate (R₂) = 21%

Time (T₁) = 8 years

Time (T₂) = 21 years

Formula Used:

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100



Calculations:

⇒ SI₁ = (P × 21 × 8) ÷ 100

⇒ SI₂ = (P × 21 × 21) ÷ 100

⇒ Required Ratio = SI₁ : SI₂

⇒ Ratio = [(P × 21 × 8) / 100] ÷ [(P × 21 × 21) / 100]

⇒ Ratio = (P × 21 × 8) ÷ (P × 21 × 21)

⇒ Ratio = 8 ÷ 21

∴ The correct answer is 8 : 21.

Additional Information

Direct Proportionality in SI

Simple interest is directly proportional to Principal, Rate, and Time individually when the other two factors remain constant.

Effective Rate of Interest

The total interest percentage for the entire period in SI is simply (Rate × Time)%. For example, 21% for 8 years is 168% of Principal.

Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

In SI, interest is only calculated on the initial principal. In CI, interest is calculated on the principal plus any accumulated interest from previous periods.

questions.q: Select the INCORRECT formula from the following options.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Identify the three standard Pythagorean trigonometric identities:

1. sin²θ + cos²θ = 1

2. sec²θ − tan²θ = 1

3. cosec²θ − cot²θ = 1

Comparing these with the options, option (3) states sec²θ + cos²θ = 1, which is mathematically incorrect.

∴ The correct answer is sec²θ + cos²θ = 1.

Alternate Method

Given: Four trigonometric formulas to verify.

Formula Used: In a right-angled triangle, Pythagoras Theorem: p² + b² = h².



⇒ Option 1: cosec²θ − cot²θ = (h/p)² − (b/p)² = (h² − b²)/p² = p²/p² = 1 (Correct)

⇒ Option 2: sin²θ + cos²θ = (p/h)² + (b/h)² = (p² + b²)/h² = h²/h² = 1 (Correct)

⇒ Option 3: sec²θ + cos²θ = (h/b)² + (b/h)² = b2h2h4+b4​ ≠ 1 (Incorrect)

⇒ Option 4: sec²θ − tan²θ = (h/b)² − (p/b)² = (h² − p²)/b² = b²/b² = 1 (Correct)

∴ The correct answer is sec²θ + cos²θ = 1.

Additional Information

Reciprocal Identities

Standard relations are sinθ × cosecθ = 1, cosθ × secθ = 1, and tanθ × cotθ = 1.

Complementary Angle Formulas

sin(90° − θ) = cosθ, tan(90° − θ) = cotθ, and sec(90° − θ) = cosecθ.

Derived Pythagorean Forms

1 + tan²θ = sec²θ and 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ.

questions.q:
Find the standard deviation of the following data (rounded off to two decimal places).

5, 3, 4, 7
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Mean (μ) = (5 + 3 + 4 + 7) ÷ 4 = 19 ÷ 4 = 4.75

Sum of squares (Σx²) = 5² + 3² + 4² + 7² = 25 + 9 + 16 + 49 = 99

Standard Deviation (σ) = √[(Σx² ÷ n) − μ²]

σ = √[(99 ÷ 4) − 4.75²] = √[24.75 − 22.5625] = √2.1875 ≈ 1.48

∴ The correct answer is 1.48.

Alternate Method

Given: Data points = {5, 3, 4, 7}, Number of observations (n) = 4

Formula Used: σ = √[Σ(xᵢ − μ)² ÷ n]



⇒ Mean (μ) = (5 + 3 + 4 + 7) ÷ 4 = 4.75

⇒ Squared deviation for 5: (5 − 4.75)² = 0.25² = 0.0625

⇒ Squared deviation for 3: (3 − 4.75)² = (−1.75)² = 3.0625

⇒ Squared deviation for 4: (4 − 4.75)² = (−0.75)² = 0.5625

⇒ Squared deviation for 7: (7 − 4.75)² = 2.25² = 5.0625

⇒ Variance (σ²) = (0.0625 + 3.0625 + 0.5625 + 5.0625) ÷ 4 = 8.75 ÷ 4 = 2.1875

⇒ Standard Deviation (σ) = √2.1875 ≈ 1.48

∴ The correct answer is 1.48.

Additional Information

Variance

Variance is the average of the squared differences from the mean, calculated as σ² = Σ(x − μ)² ÷ n.

Coefficient of Variation (CV)

It is a relative measure of dispersion calculated as CV = (σ ÷ μ) × 100%.

Range

Range is the simplest measure of dispersion, defined as the difference between the maximum and minimum values in a dataset.

questions.q: Suresh, Dinesh and Ramesh became partners in a business by investing money in the ratio of 3 : 6 : 8. If their investments is increased by 5%, 15% and 20%, respectively, then what will be the ratio of their profits for one year?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Let the initial investments be 300, 600, and 800 units.

Suresh's new investment = 300 + 5% of 300 = 315.

Dinesh's new investment = 600 + 15% of 600 = 690.

Ramesh's new investment = 800 + 20% of 800 = 960.

New Profit Ratio = 315 : 690 : 960 = 21 : 46 : 64 (divided by 15).

∴ The correct answer is 21 ∶ 46 ∶ 64.

Alternate Method

Given:

Investment ratio (S : D : R) = 3 : 6 : 8

Percentage increases = 5%, 15%, 20%

Time period = 1 year (Constant for all)

Formula Used: Profit Ratio = (Investment₁ × Time₁) : (Investment₂ × Time₂) : (Investment₃ × Time₃)



Calculations:

⇒ Let initial investments be 3x, 6x, and 8x.

⇒ New investment of Suresh = 3x × (100 + 5)/100 = 3x × 1.05 = 3.15x

⇒ New investment of Dinesh = 6x × (100 + 15)/100 = 6x × 1.15 = 6.90x

⇒ New investment of Ramesh = 8x × (100 + 20)/100 = 8x × 1.20 = 9.60x

⇒ Ratio of profits = 3.15x : 6.90x : 9.60x

⇒ Multiplying by 100 to remove decimals: 315 : 690 : 960

⇒ Dividing each term by 15:

⇒ Suresh = 315 ÷ 15 = 21

⇒ Dinesh = 690 ÷ 15 = 46

⇒ Ramesh = 960 ÷ 15 = 64

∴ The correct answer is 21 ∶ 46 ∶ 64.

Additional Information

Partnership Profit Sharing Rule

Profit is always distributed in the ratio of the product of Capital and Time (P = C × T). If Time is constant, Profit Ratio = Capital Ratio.

Percentage Change in Ratio

If a value 'a' increases by r%, the new value is a × (1 + r/100). This can be applied directly to ratio terms.

Simplifying Ratios

To simplify a ratio involving decimals, multiply all terms by a power of 10 to convert them to integers and then divide by their HCF.

questions.q: The ratio of marks obtained by Rajesh, Rakesh and Ramesh in an exam is 2 : 4 : 9. What are the marks obtained by Rakesh and Ramesh, if Rajesh scored 30 marks in the exam?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of Rajesh : Rakesh : Ramesh = 2 : 4 : 9

Given: Rajesh (2 units) = 30 marks

Unit value = 30 ÷ 2 = 15 marks

Rakesh (4 units) = 4 × 15 = 60 marks

Ramesh (9 units) = 9 × 15 = 135 marks

∴ The correct answer is Rakesh = 60, Ramesh = 135.

Alternate Method

Given:

Ratio of marks = 2 : 4 : 9

Marks scored by Rajesh = 30

Formula:

Value of one ratio part = Given value ÷ Corresponding ratio share



⇒ Let the marks of Rajesh, Rakesh, and Ramesh be 2x, 4x, and 9x respectively.

⇒ 2x = 30

⇒ x = 30 ÷ 2 = 15

⇒ Rakesh's marks = 4x = 4 × 15 = 60

⇒ Ramesh's marks = 9x = 9 × 15 = 135

∴ The correct answer is Rakesh = 60, Ramesh = 135.

Additional Information

Ratio Definition

A ratio compares quantities by division and is usually expressed in its simplest form (a : b).

Unitary Method in Ratios

Total value = (Sum of ratio parts) × (Value of one part). Conversely, Value of one part = Given value ÷ Respective ratio part.

Proportion

Equality of two ratios is called proportion. If a : b :: c : d, then product of extremes (ad) = product of means (bc).

questions.q: The average of 20 numbers is 32. If two numbers are 29 and 31, then what is the average of the remaining numbers (correct up to two decimals)?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Initial average of 20 numbers = 32.

Numbers removed = 29 and 31 (Total = 60).

Deviation from average = (29 − 32) + (31 − 32) = −3 + (−1) = −4.

Since the removed sum (60) is less than the expected sum (32 × 2 = 64), the average will increase.

Net increase in average = 4 ÷ 18 ≈ 0.22.

New average = 32 + 0.22 = 32.22.

∴ The correct answer is 32.22.

Alternate Method

Given:

Total numbers (n₁) = 20

Initial average (A₁) = 32

Numbers to be removed = 29 and 31

Formula: Average = Sum of observations ÷ Number of observations



Calculations:

⇒ Total sum of 20 numbers = 20 × 32 = 640

⇒ Sum of the two removed numbers = 29 + 31 = 60

⇒ Sum of the remaining numbers = 640 − 60 = 580

⇒ Total remaining numbers = 20 − 2 = 18

⇒ Average of remaining numbers = 580 ÷ 18

⇒ Average = 290 ÷ 9 = 32.222...

∴ The correct answer is 32.22.

Additional Information

Average of First n Natural Numbers

The average of the first n natural numbers is given by the formula (n + 1) ÷ 2.

Effect of Replacement on Average

When a value x is replaced by y, the New Average = Old Average + (y − x) ÷ Total Count.

Weighted Average

For two groups with averages A₁, A₂ and counts n₁, n₂, the combined average is (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

questions.q: The angle of elevation of the top of a building at a distance of 70 m from its foot on a horizontal plane is found to be 60°. Find the height of the building.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

In a 30°−60°−90° right-angled triangle, the ratio of sides opposite to the angles is 1 : √3 : 2.

Base (opposite to 30°) = 70 m.

Height (opposite to 60°) = Base × √3.

Height = 70 × √3 = 70√3 m.

∴ The correct answer is 70√3 m.

Alternate Method

Given:

Distance from the foot (Base) = 70 m

Angle of elevation (θ) = 60°

Formula Used:

tan θ = Perpendicular (Height) ÷ Base



Calculations:

⇒ tan 60° = h ÷ 70

⇒ √3 = h ÷ 70

⇒ h = 70 × √3

⇒ h = 70√3 m

∴ The correct answer is 70√3 m.

Additional Information

Trigonometric Values for Heights & Distances

tan 30° = 1/√3, tan 45° = 1, and tan 60° = √3 are the most frequently used ratios in elevation problems.

Angle of Elevation and Depression

The angle of elevation from an observer's eye to an object is numerically equal to the angle of depression from the object to the observer due to alternate interior angles.

30-60-90 Triangle Theorem

In any 30°−60°−90° triangle, the hypotenuse is twice the shorter leg, and the longer leg is √3 times the shorter leg.

questions.q: ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral and BC is a diameter of the related circle on which A and D also lie. ∠BCA = 19° and ∠CAD = 32°. What is the measure of ∠ACD?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

In a cyclic quadrilateral with diameter BC, ∠BAC = 90°.

∠BAD = ∠BAC + ∠CAD = 90° + 32° = 122°.

Since ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral, ∠BAD + ∠BCD = 180°.

∴ ∠BCD = 180° − 122° = 58°.

∠ACD = ∠BCD − ∠BCA = 58° − 19° = 39°.

∴ The correct answer is 39°.

Alternate Method

Given: BC is diameter, ∠BCA = 19°, ∠CAD = 32°.

Formula Used: Angle in a semi-circle is 90°; Sum of opposite angles in a cyclic quadrilateral is 180°.



⇒ In &xot;ABC, since BC is the diameter, ∠BAC = 90° (Angle in a semi-circle).

⇒ ∠BAD = ∠BAC + ∠CAD = 90° + 32° = 122°.

⇒ For cyclic quadrilateral ABCD, ∠BAD + ∠BCD = 180°.

⇒ 122° + ∠BCD = 180°.

⇒ ∠BCD = 180° − 122° = 58°.

⇒ We know ∠BCD = ∠BCA + ∠ACD.

⇒ 58° = 19° + ∠ACD.

⇒ ∠ACD = 58° − 19° = 39°.

∴ The correct answer is 39°.

Additional Information

Angle in a Semi-circle

An angle subtended by the diameter of a circle at any point on the circumference is always a right angle (90°).

Cyclic Quadrilateral Property

The sum of opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral is always 180° (∠A + ∠C = 180° and ∠B + ∠D = 180°).

Angles in the Same Segment

Angles subtended by the same arc at the circumference of the circle are equal. For example, ∠ADB = ∠ACB.

questions.q: Find the single equivalent discount for successive discounts of 12%, 18% and 25% on the marked price of a car.
questions.solution:
Method:
1. Assume the Marked Price (MP) is 100.
2. Apply 1st discount (12%): 100×0.88=88.
3. Apply 2nd discount (18%): 88×0.82=72.16.
4. Apply 3rd discount (25%): 72.16×0.75=54.12.
5. Calculate Total Discount: 100−54.12=45.88.

Explanation:
Successive discounts are applied to the reduced value of the previous step, not the original price. To find the final price quickly, multiply the remaining percentage (multiplying factor) of each discount. The single equivalent discount is the total reduction from the original 100%.

Why the others are wrong:
(A) 35.28% is incorrect as it likely results from adding discounts incorrectly.
(B) 42.65% is incorrect and does not follow the successive reduction rule.
(C) 40.25% is incorrect as it fails to account for the compounding effect of the 18% and 25% discounts.

questions.q: Rewa has some hens and some goats. If the total number of animal heads is 100 and the total number of animal feet is 348, then what is the total number of goats with Rewa?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Assume all 100 animals are hens (2 feet each).

Total feet would be: 100 × 2 = 200 feet.

Excess feet count: 348 − 200 = 148 feet.

Each goat has 2 extra feet compared to a hen (4 − 2 = 2).

Total goats = 148 ÷ 2 = 74 goats.

∴ The correct answer is 74 goats.

Alternate Method

Given:

Total number of heads = 100

Total number of feet = 348

Formula Used:

H + G = Total Heads; 2H + 4G = Total Feet (where H = Hens, G = Goats)



Calculations:

⇒ Average feet per head = 348 ÷ 100 = 3.48

⇒ By Alligation method, Ratio of Hens to Goats = (4 − 3.48) : (3.48 − 2)

⇒ Ratio (Hens : Goats) = 0.52 : 1.48 = 13 : 37

⇒ Total units = 13 + 37 = 50 units

⇒ 50 units = 100 animals

⇒ 1 unit = 2 animals

⇒ Total Goats = 37 × 2 = 74

∴ The correct answer is 74 goats.

Additional Information

Direct Formula for 4-legged animals

Number of 4-legged animals = (Total feet − 2 × Total heads) ÷ 2. This is derived from linear substitution.

Weighted Average Principle

The mean value (3.48) always lies between the two extremes (2 and 4). The closer the mean is to one extreme, the higher the proportion of that category.

System of Linear Equations

Problems involving two variables and two conditions (like heads and feet) can always be solved using the substitution or elimination method.

questions.q: If the external angle of a regular polygon is 18°, then the number of diagonals in this polygon is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Number of sides in regular polygon = 360° ÷ Exterior angle

Number of sides = 360° ÷ 18° = 20

Number of diagonals = [Sides × (Sides − 3)] ÷ 2

Number of diagonals = [20 × (20 − 3)] ÷ 2 = 10 × 17 = 170

∴ The correct answer is 170.

Alternate Method

Given:

Exterior angle of a regular polygon = 18°

Formula Used:

1. Number of sides (n) = 360° ÷ Exterior angle

2. Number of diagonals = n × (n − 3) ÷ 2



Calculations:

⇒ Number of sides (n) = 360° ÷ 18°

⇒ n = 20

⇒ Number of diagonals = 20 × (20 − 3) ÷ 2

⇒ Number of diagonals = 20 × 17 ÷ 2

⇒ Number of diagonals = 10 × 17 = 170

∴ The correct answer is 170.

Additional Information

Sum of Exterior Angles

For any convex polygon with n sides, the sum of all exterior angles is always 360°.

Sum of Interior Angles

The sum of all interior angles of a polygon with n sides is given by (n − 2) × 180°.

Relationship between Angles

At each vertex of a polygon, the sum of the interior angle and the exterior angle is 180°.

Number of Diagonals Formula

The number of diagonals is calculated as ⁿC₂ − n, which simplifies to n(n − 3) ÷ 2.

questions.q: The number 2918245 is divisible by which of the following numbers?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Check divisibility by sum of digits: 2 + 9 + 1 + 8 + 2 + 4 + 5 = 31 (Not divisible by 3 or 9).

Check divisibility by 4: Last two digits are 45 (Not divisible by 4, so not by 12).

Check divisibility by 11: Alternating sum = 2 − 9 + 1 − 8 + 2 − 4 + 5 = −11.

Since 11 is divisible by 11, the entire number is divisible by 11.

∴ The correct answer is 11.

Alternate Method

Given: Number = 2918245

Method: Apply divisibility rules for each option.



Checking each option:

⇒ Divisibility by 3: Sum of digits = 2+9+1+8+2+4+5 = 31. Since 31 is not divisible by 3, the number is not divisible by 3.

⇒ Divisibility by 9: Since the sum 31 is not divisible by 9, the number is not divisible by 9.

⇒ Divisibility by 12: A number is divisible by 12 if it is divisible by both 3 and 4. Since it is not divisible by 3, it cannot be divisible by 12.

⇒ Divisibility by 11: Sum of digits at odd places (from right) = 5 + 2 + 1 + 2 = 10. Sum of digits at even places (from right) = 4 + 8 + 9 = 21.

⇒ Difference = |21 − 10| = 11. Since 11 is divisible by 11, the number 2918245 is divisible by 11.

∴ The correct answer is 11.

Additional Information

Divisibility by 3 and 9

A number is divisible by 3 or 9 if the sum of its digits is divisible by 3 or 9, respectively.

Divisibility by 4 and 8

A number is divisible by 4 if its last two digits are divisible by 4, and by 8 if its last three digits are divisible by 8.

Divisibility by 11 Rule

The difference between the sum of digits at odd places and the sum of digits at even places must be 0 or a multiple of 11.

Divisibility by 6

A number is divisible by 6 if it is divisible by both 2 (even number) and 3 (sum of digits rule).

questions.q: The average weight of three men is increased by 4 kg when one of them, whose weight is 100 kg, is replaced by another man. What is the weight of the new man?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

New Weight = Replaced Weight + (Total Number × Change in Average)

Here, Replaced weight = 100 kg, Number of men = 3, Average increase = 4 kg

New man weight = 100 + (3 × 4)

New man weight = 100 + 12 = 112 kg

∴ The correct answer is 112 kg.

Alternate Method

Given:

Number of men = 3

Weight of the man replaced = 100 kg

Increase in average weight = 4 kg

Formula Used:

Weight of new person = Weight of replaced person + (Total persons × Increase in average)



⇒ Total weight of 3 men = 3 × Average weight (A)

⇒ Let the weights of the men be M₁, M₂, and 100 kg.

⇒ (M₁ + M₂ + 100) ÷ 3 = A

⇒ (M₁ + M₂ + New Man) ÷ 3 = A + 4

⇒ M₁ + M₂ + New Man = 3A + 12

⇒ Since M₁ + M₂ + 100 = 3A, then M₁ + M₂ = 3A − 100

⇒ (3A − 100) + New Man = 3A + 12

⇒ New Man = 3A + 12 − 3A + 100

⇒ New Man = 112 kg

∴ The correct answer is 112 kg.

Additional Information

General Replacement Rule

When one person is replaced, New Value = Old Value + (Total Count × Increase) or New Value = Old Value − (Total Count × Decrease).

Average of Group

Average = Sum of all observations ÷ Number of observations. If the average increases, the incoming value must be greater than the outgoing value.

Effect of Adding a Member

When a person is added (not replaced), the total count increases. New Total Weight = (Old Average × Old Count) + New Member Weight.

questions.q:
The median of the following data will be _.

questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Arrange the data in ascending order: 25, 27, 29, 30, 32, 33, 35.

The number of terms (n) = 7, which is an odd number.

For an odd number of terms, the median is the middle-most value.

The middle term is the 4th term in the sorted list.

The 4th term is 30.

∴ The correct answer is 30.

Alternate Method

Given: Data set = {32, 25, 33, 27, 35, 29, 30}

Formula Used: Median = [(n + 1) / 2]th term, where n is the number of observations (when n is odd).



⇒ Count the number of observations in the data set:

⇒ n = 7 (which is odd)

⇒ Arrange the data in ascending order: 25, 27, 29, 30, 32, 33, 35

⇒ Median = [(7 + 1) / 2]th observation

⇒ Median = 8 / 2 = 4th observation

⇒ The 4th observation in the sorted list is 30.

∴ The correct answer is 30.

Additional Information

Median for Even n

When the number of observations (n) is even, the median is calculated as the average of the (n/2)th and (n/2 + 1)th terms.

Importance of Sorting

The data must always be arranged in either ascending or descending order before identifying the middle term; otherwise, the result will be incorrect.

Range of Data

The range is the difference between the maximum and minimum values: Range = Max − Min. For this data, Range = 35 − 25 = 10.

questions.q: A hemispherical bowl of internal radius 18 cm is full of liquid. This liquid is to be filled in cylindrical bottles each of radius 3 cm and height 6 cm. How many bottles are required to empty the bowl?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Number of bottles (n) = Volume of bowl ÷ Volume of one bottle

n = [(2/3) × π × R³] ÷ [π × r² × h]

n = [2 × 18 × 18 × 18] ÷ [3 × 3 × 3 × 6]

n = (2 × 6 × 6) = 72 bottles

∴ The correct answer is 72 bottles.

Alternate Method

Given:

Internal radius of hemispherical bowl (R) = 18 cm

Radius of cylindrical bottle (r) = 3 cm

Height of cylindrical bottle (h) = 6 cm

Formula Used:

Volume of hemisphere = (2/3) × π × R³

Volume of cylinder = π × r² × h



Calculations:

⇒ Volume of liquid in bowl = (2/3) × π × (18)³ cm³

⇒ Volume of one bottle = π × (3)² × 6 cm³

⇒ Let n be the number of bottles required.

⇒ n × (Volume of one bottle) = Volume of bowl

⇒ n × (π × 3 × 3 × 6) = (2/3) × π × 18 × 18 × 18

⇒ n = (2 × π × 18 × 18 × 18) ÷ (3 × π × 9 × 6)

⇒ n = (2 × 5832) ÷ (162)

⇒ n = 11664 ÷ 162

⇒ n = 72

∴ The correct answer is 72 bottles.

Additional Information

Total Surface Area (TSA) of Hemisphere

The TSA of a solid hemisphere includes the curved area and the flat circular base, given by 3πr².

Volume of Sphere

The volume of a complete sphere is double that of a hemisphere, calculated as (4/3)πr³.

Surface Area of Cylinder

Curved Surface Area = 2πrh and Total Surface Area = 2πr(h + r).

questions.q: Products pass successively through the hands of three traders and each of them sells his goods at a profit of 30% of his cost price. If the last trader sold the products for Rs.300, then how much did the first trader pay for them?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Each trader adds 30% profit, so the Multiplying Factor (MF) for each sale = 1.3

Successive MF for three traders = 1.3 × 1.3 × 1.3 = 2.197

Final Selling Price = Initial Cost Price × 2.197

300 = Initial CP × 2.197

Initial CP = 300 ÷ 2.197 ≈ 136.55

∴ The correct answer is Rs.136.55 (approx).

Alternate Method

Given:

Profit of each trader = 30%

Number of traders = 3

Final Selling Price = Rs.300

Formula Used:

Selling Price (SP) = Cost Price (CP) × (1 + Profit%/100)



Let the amount the first trader paid (initial Cost Price) be x.

⇒ CP of second trader (SP of first trader) = x × (1 + 30/100) = 1.3x

⇒ CP of third trader (SP of second trader) = 1.3x × 1.3 = 1.69x

⇒ Final Selling Price (SP of third trader) = 1.69x × 1.3 = 2.197x

⇒ According to the question, 2.197x = 300

⇒ x = 300 ÷ 2.197

⇒ x = 136.5498...

⇒ x ≈ 136.55

∴ The correct answer is Rs.136.55 (approx).

Additional Information

Successive Percentage Change

When a value changes successively by a%, b%, and c%, the final value is Initial × (1 + a/100) × (1 + b/100) × (1 + c/100).

Net Profit Percentage

The equivalent single profit percentage for three successive profits of p% is given by [(1 + p/100)³ − 1] × 100.

Effective Rate for Two Changes

For two successive changes of a% and b%, the net change is (a + b + ab/100)%.

questions.q: What is the total surface area of a pyramid whose base is a square with side 8 cm and height of the pyramid is 3 cm?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Slant height (l) = √(Height² + (Side/2)²) = √(3² + 4²) = 5 cm.

Base Area = Side² = 8² = 64 cm².

Lateral Area = 2 × Side × Slant height = 2 × 8 × 5 = 80 cm².

Total Surface Area (TSA) = 64 + 80 = 144 cm².

∴ The correct answer is 144 cm².

Alternate Method

Given: Base side (a) = 8 cm, Height of pyramid (h) = 3 cm.

Formula: TSA = Base Area + 1/2 × Perimeter × Slant Height (l)



⇒ Area of square base = a² = 8 × 8 = 64 cm²

⇒ Slant height (l) = √(h² + (a/2)²)

⇒ l = √(3² + 4²) = √(9 + 16) = √25 = 5 cm

⇒ Perimeter of base = 4 × a = 4 × 8 = 32 cm

⇒ Lateral Surface Area (LSA) = 1/2 × 32 × 5 = 16 × 5 = 80 cm²

⇒ Total Surface Area (TSA) = Base Area + LSA

⇒ TSA = 64 + 80 = 144 cm²

∴ The correct answer is 144 cm².

Additional Information

Volume of a Pyramid

The volume is given by V = 1/3 × Base Area × Vertical Height.

Slant Height vs Slant Edge

Slant height (l) is the height of the triangular face, while Slant edge (e) = √(h² + (d/2)²) where d is the diagonal of the base.

Regular Pyramid Properties

In a regular pyramid, all lateral faces are congruent isosceles triangles and the apex is directly above the center of the base.

Diagonal of a Cube

questions.q: What is the simplified form of the expression (1+x)(1+x²)(1+x⁴)(1+x⁸)(1-x)?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Identify the telescoping pattern of the identity (a − b)(a + b) = a² − b².

Each pair of terms doubles the power of x: (1 − xⁿ)(1 + xⁿ) = 1 − x²ⁿ.

The sequence starts with power 1 and ends with power 8.

The final simplified power will be the highest power in the product multiplied by 2.

Highest power is 8, so final result is 1 − x⁸ × ² = 1 − x¹⁶.

∴ The correct answer is 1 − x¹⁶.

Alternate Method

Given Expression: (1 + x)(1 + x²)(1 + x⁴)(1 + x⁸)(1 − x)

Formula: (a − b)(a + b) = a² − b²

⇒ Rearranging the terms to group conjugates:

⇒ [(1 − x)(1 + x)] × (1 + x²) × (1 + x⁴) × (1 + x⁸)

⇒ (1 − x²) × (1 + x²) × (1 + x⁴) × (1 + x⁸)

⇒ [(1 − x²)(1 + x²)] × (1 + x⁴) × (1 + x⁸)

⇒ (1 − x⁴) × (1 + x⁴) × (1 + x⁸)

⇒ [(1 − x⁴)(1 + x⁴)] × (1 + x⁸)

⇒ (1 − x⁸) × (1 + x⁸)

⇒ 1 − (x⁸)²

⇒ 1 − x¹⁶

∴ The correct answer is 1 − x¹⁶.

Additional Information

Difference of Squares Identity

The algebraic identity (a + b)(a − b) = a² − b² is fundamental for simplifying products of binomial conjugates.

Exponents Rule

When raising a power to another power, the exponents are multiplied: (xa)b = xa × b.

General Telescoping Form

The general product (1 − x)(1 + x)(1 + x²)(1 + x⁴)...(1 + x²ⁿ) simplifies to 1 − x²ⁿ⁺¹.

questions.q: If the areas of two similar triangles are in the ratio 196 : 625, what would be the ratio of the corresponding sides?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For two similar triangles, the ratio of their areas is equal to the square of the ratio of their corresponding sides.

Ratio of sides = √(Ratio of Areas)

Ratio of sides = √196 : √625

Ratio of sides = 14 : 25

∴ The correct answer is 14 : 25.

Alternate Method

Given:

Ratio of areas of two similar triangles = 196 : 625

Formula used:

If ΔABC ∼ ΔPQR, then Area(ΔABC) ÷ Area(ΔPQR) = (AB ÷ PQ)² = (BC ÷ QR)² = (AC ÷ PR)²



Let the corresponding sides of the two triangles be s₁ and s₂.

Let the areas of the two triangles be A₁ and A₂.

⇒ A₁ ÷ A₂ = (s₁ ÷ s₂)²

⇒ 196 ÷ 625 = (s₁ ÷ s₂)²

⇒ s₁ ÷ s₂ = √(196 ÷ 625)

⇒ s₁ ÷ s₂ = 14 ÷ 25

⇒ s₁ : s₂ = 14 : 25

∴ The correct answer is 14 : 25.

Additional Information

Properties of Similar Triangles

The ratio of the perimeters of two similar triangles is equal to the ratio of their corresponding sides: P₁/P₂ = s₁/s₂.

Ratio of Altitudes and Medians

The ratio of corresponding altitudes, medians, or angle bisectors of two similar triangles is also equal to the ratio of their corresponding sides.

Area Theorem

The theorem states that for two similar triangles, the ratio of their areas is the square of the ratio of any two corresponding linear dimensions.

questions.q: A speaks the truth 5 out of 7 times and B speaks truth 8 out of 9 times. What is the probability that they contradict each other in stating the same fact?
options: 71​
91​
41​
31​
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Probability A speaks truth = 5/7, Lie = 2/7

Probability B speaks truth = 8/9, Lie = 1/9

Contradiction = (ATᵣᵤₜₕ × BLᵢₑ) + (ALᵢₑ × BTᵣᵤₜₕ)

⇒ (5/7 × 1/9) + (2/7 × 8/9) = (5 + 16) / 63 = 21/63 = 1/3

∴ The correct answer is 1/3.

Alternate Method

Given:

Probability of A speaking truth, P(A) = 5/7

Probability of B speaking truth, P(B) = 8/9

Formula:

Probability of contradiction = P(A ∩ B′) + P(A′ ∩ B)



Probability that A lies, P(A′) = 1 − P(A) = 1 − 5/7 = 2/7

Probability that B lies, P(B′) = 1 − P(B) = 1 − 8/9 = 1/9

They contradict each other if one speaks truth and the other speaks lie.

⇒ Required Probability = [P(A) × P(B′)] + [P(A′) × P(B)]

⇒ Required Probability = (5/7 × 1/9) + (2/7 × 8/9)

⇒ Required Probability = 5/63 + 16/63

⇒ Required Probability = 21/63

⇒ Required Probability = 1/3

∴ The correct answer is 1/3.

Additional Information

Independent Events

Two events A and B are independent if the occurrence of one does not affect the other, then P(A ∩ B) = P(A) × P(B).

Complementary Events

The probability of an event not occurring is P(A′) = 1 − P(A).

Probability of Agreement

The probability that they agree with each other is P(A)P(B) + P(A′)P(B′), which is also equal to 1 − P(Contradict).

questions.q: There are two inlet pipes A and B connected to a tank. A and B can fill the tank in 32 h and 28 h, respectively. If both the pipes are opened alternately for 1 h, starting with A, then in how much time (in hours, to nearest integer) will the tank be filled?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total work (LCM of 32 and 28) = 224 units.

Efficiency: A = 7 units/h, B = 8 units/h.

Work done in 1 cycle of 2 hours (A + B) = 7 + 8 = 15 units.

In 14 cycles (28 hours), work completed = 14 × 15 = 210 units.

Remaining work = 224 − 210 = 14 units. In 29th hour, A fills 7 units. Remaining 7 units filled by B in 7/8 hours.

Total time = 29.875 hours ≈ 30 hours.

∴ The correct answer is 30 h.

Alternate Method

Given: Time taken by A = 32 h, Time taken by B = 28 h.

Formula: Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

Pipes and Cisterns General Formula

Efficiency and Time Relationship

questions.q: Two candidates contested an election. One of them got 64% of the votes and won by 434 votes. What was the total number of votes polled?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

The winning candidate got 64% of the total votes.

The losing candidate got (100% − 64%) = 36% of the total votes.

Difference in vote percentage = 64% − 36% = 28%

Given, 28% of total votes = 434

Total votes = 434 × (100 ÷ 28) = 1550

∴ The correct answer is 1550.

Alternate Method

Votes polled by the winning candidate = 64%

Winning margin = 434 votes

Total votes percentage = 100%

Total Votes = 100%

Winner (64%)

28% → 434 votes

Calculations:

⇒ Votes polled by the losing candidate = 100% − 64% = 36%

⇒ Difference in percentage = 64% − 36% = 28%

Since the winning margin is 434 votes:

⇒ 28% of Total Votes = 434

⇒ 1% of Total Votes = 434 ÷ 28 = 15.5

⇒ Total Votes (100%) = 15.5 × 100 = 1550

∴ The correct answer is 1550.

Additional Information

Valid and Invalid Votes

When certain votes are declared invalid, the percentage calculations are usually based on valid votes. Total Valid Votes = Total Votes Polled − Invalid Votes.

Percentage Change and Base

In election problems, percentages are calculated with respect to the total voter base unless stated otherwise. The winning margin is always the difference in percentages between the winner and the loser.

Successive Percentage Shift

When counting the active voting population: Final Valid Votes = Total Registered Voters × (1 − Non-voters%) × (1 − Invalid%).

questions.q: From the top of an upright pole 17.75 m high, the angle of elevation of the top of an upright tower was 60⁰. If the tower was 57.75 m tall, how far away (in m) from the foot of the pole was the foot of the tower?

Shortcut Trick

The side opposite to 60° is √3 units, and the base (distance) is 1 unit.

Distance = (40/√3) × (√3/√3) = 40√3/3 m.

∴ The correct answer is 40√3/3 m.

Alternate Method

Given:

Height of pole (AB) = 17.75 m

Height of tower (CD) = 57.75 m

Angle of elevation from top of pole to top of tower (θ) = 60°



Formula Used:

In a right-angled triangle, tan θ = Perpendicular / Base

Calculations:

The height of the tower above the pole level (DE) = CD − AB

⇒ tan 60° = DE / AE

⇒ √3 = 40 / x

⇒ x = 40 / √3

To rationalize the denominator, multiply and divide by √3:

⇒ x = (40 × √3) / (√3 × √3)

⇒ x = 40√3 / 3 m

∴ The correct answer is 40√3/3 m.

Additional Information

Angle of Elevation

The angle formed by the line of sight with the horizontal when looking up at an object. tan θ = Height / Distance.

Trigonometric Ratios for Standard Angles

tan 30° = 1/√3, tan 45° = 1, tan 60° = √3.

30°-60°-90° Triangle Rule

Sides are in the ratio 1 : √3 : 2. Side opposite 30° is x, side opposite 60° is x√3, and hypotenuse is 2x.

questions.q:
In this question, a statement is followed by two courses of action, numbered I and II. You must assume everything in the statement to be true and on the basis of the information given in the statement, decide which course of action/s logically follows for pursuing.

Statement: There is a large increase in migration of villagers to urban areas as repeated crop failure has put them into financial problems.

Course of action:

I. The villagers should be provided with an alternate source of income in their villages which will make them stay there only.

II. To ensure their survival, the migrated villagers should be given access to all housing options in urban areas.
questions.solution:
The given statement highlights the reason for the large increase in migration of villagers to urban areas. Based on this, we can evaluate the two courses of action:

Course of action I: The villagers should be provided with an alternate source of income in their villages which will make them stay there only. This course of action seems logical and appropriate as providing an alternate source of income in their villages would help them stay in their villages instead of migrating to urban areas. This can also help in reducing the pressure on urban areas and improving the overall living conditions of the villagers in their own villages.

Course of action II: To ensure their survival, the migrated villagers should be given access to all housing options in urban areas. This course of action is not a practical solution as providing access to all housing options in urban areas may not be possible for the authorities. It may also not solve the root cause of the problem, which is the repeated crop failure leading to financial problems. Moreover, providing housing options to migrants may lead to the creation of slums and other social problems in urban areas.

Therefore, only course of action I logically follows for pursuing.

A. Then a nurse and a doctor came

B. After the terrible accident

C. A car took Raman to the hospital

D. The two men carried him to a bed and put him in it carefully
questions.solution:
Method:
1. Identify the opening phrase by looking for a time indicator or a starting event.
2. Look for the logical sequence of events: Accident → Transport → Arrival → Action.
3. Connect the subject (Raman) to the consequence (the hospital).
4. Match the sequence with the given options.

Explanation:
The paragraph follows a chronological order. It starts with the cause (B: After the terrible accident), followed by the immediate action (C: A car took Raman to the hospital). Once at the hospital, the next step is the arrival of medical staff (A: Then a nurse and a doctor came), and finally, the action they performed (D: The two men carried him to a bed).

Why the others are wrong:
(A) DCBA is wrong because it starts with an action before the accident even happened.
(B) ABCD is wrong because it places the arrival of the doctor before the accident occurred.
(D) ACDB is wrong because it lacks a logical starting point and breaks the timeline.

questions.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

Marvel Comics created Superman.
options: Superman was created by Marvel Comics.
Superman is created by Marvel Comics.
questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is Superman was created by Marvel Comics.

Key Points

• The above-given sentence is in the active voice.

• We need to change it in the passive voice.

• The following steps are required to change the given sentence into passive voice:-

• The subject 'Marvel Comics' of the active voice will become the object of the passive voice.

• The object 'Superman' of the active voice will become the subject of the passive voice.

• The tense(simple past tense) will change according to the following structure:-

• Active Voice - Subject + (did + V1) or (V2) + Object.

• Passive Voice - Object + was/were + V3 + by + Subject.

• ​Thus, the correct answer is Option 1.

Therefore, the correct passive voice is *Superman was created by Marvel Comics.*

Additional Information

• When we convert active voice to passive voice, three things need to be kept in mind:-

• Change object into subject.

• Change subject into object.

• Always use the third form of the verb in the passive voice.

• Use 'by' before the new object.

Why the others are wrong:
(A) "smarty and strong" is grammatically incorrect as it mixes an informal noun/adjective with a base adjective.
(B) "smartest and strongest" is the Superlative Degree, used for comparing more than two things, not with "than".
(D) "smart and strong" is the Positive Degree, which cannot be used directly with the word "than".

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Overt.

Key Points

• The word "clandestine" means kept secret or done secretively, especially because illicit. (गुप्त, गुप्त रूप से किया गया)

• Example: They held a clandestine meeting to discuss the secret plans.

• The antonym of "clandestine" is "Overt", which means done or shown openly; plainly apparent. (स्पष्ट, खुला)

• Example: The company’s overt support for environmental causes was well-documented.

Therefore, the most appropriate antonym for the underlined word "clandestine" is Option 2 i.e. Overt.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and why they are not suitable antonyms:

• Surreptitious (गुप्त रूप): Kept secret, especially because it would not be approved of.

• Example: They conducted a surreptitious investigation.

• Not suitable because "surreptitious" is a synonym of "clandestine," not an antonym.

• Example: He made amorous advances towards her.

questions.q:

options: A difficult situation in which the solution to a problem is impossible
A positive outcome in a tough situation
questions.solution:
The correct answer is A difficult situation in which the solution to a problem is impossible.

Key Points

• The most appropriate meaning of the idiom "Catch 22 situation" is option 2) "A difficult situation in which the solution to a problem is impossible."

• The term "Catch-22" originated from the title of a novel by Joseph Heller, which portrays a situation where an individual is caught in a contradictory or paradoxical situation, where the solution to one problem creates another problem that makes it impossible to proceed.

• For example, if a person wants to get a job but needs experience to get a job, they are in a Catch-22 situation because they can't get the job without experience and they can't gain experience without the job.

• In the given sentence, the manager is in a Catch-22 situation, which means the manager is facing a difficult problem where the solution leads to another problem that makes it impossible to solve.

• Therefore, the most appropriate meaning of the highlighted idiom in the given sentence is "a difficult situation in which the solution to a problem is impossible."

questions.q:

B. The melting of the ice caps will increase the sea level, thereby drowning many islands and coastal regions.

C. The increased amount of carbon emission is considered as the reason behind global warming.

D. The increase in the global temperature is melting the polar ice caps.
questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is ACDB.

Key Points

• A) The sentence "The temperature of the world has increased, resulting in global warming*" *provides the context for the paragraph by stating that global warming is the main subject of the paragraph.

• C) The sentence "The increased amount of carbon emission is considered as the reason behind global warming" provides the cause for global warming, which is due to the increased amount of carbon emission in the atmosphere.

• D) The sentence "The increase in the global temperature is melting the polar ice caps" explains how the increase in global temperature is causing the polar ice caps to melt.

• B) The sentence "The melting of the ice caps will increase the sea level, thereby drowning many islands and coastal regions" explains the consequences of the polar ice caps melting, which will lead to an increase in sea level, causing the drowning of many islands and coastal regions.

• Therefore, the correct order of the sentences to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph is ACDB.

questions.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

“So help me heaven!”, the man cried, “I shall never lie again.”
options: The man cries out to heaven to help him not to lie again ever.
The man called upon heaven to witness his resolve that he would never lie again.
The man requested heaven to help him and see that he lie again.
The man called heaven and ordered to help him and see to it that she never lies again.
questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is The man called upon heaven to witness his resolve that he would never lie again.

Key Points

• The given sentence is in Direct Speech. As per the given directions, we have to change it into Indirect Speech.

• As the given sentence is an exclamatory sentence, the process of transformation is as follows:

• In the Indirect speech 'cried' will be changed into 'called upon heaven' because reporting speech has an exclamation.

• The indirect speech will begin like 'The man called upon heaven to.'

• 'To' will be followed by the first form of the verb 'witness'.

• Now we have to change the reported speech.

• Here 'I' will be changed into 'he.'

• The modal verb 'shall' will change into 'would'.

• Finally, the indirect speech is 'The man called upon heaven to witness his resolve that he would never lie again.'

• ​So, the correct answer is option 2.

• Option 1 changes the tense of the verbs incorrectly (present tense) and does not accurately reflect the meaning of the original sentence.

• Option 3 changes the meaning of the sentence and does not accurately reflect the man's statement.

• Option 4 is incorrect because the man was not ordering the heaven.

Correct Indirect Speech: *The man called upon heaven to witness his resolve that he would never lie again.*

questions.solution:
Method:
1. Identify the reporting verb "inquired" and change it to said to me (since it's a question).
2. Identify the tense change: "was doing" (Past Continuous) must change back to are doing (Present Continuous) for direct speech.
3. Identify the pronoun change: "I" (the subject) becomes you, and "my" (the possessor) becomes your.
4. Reconstruct the interrogative structure: How + auxiliary verb + subject.

Explanation:
The original sentence is an indirect interrogative sentence (Wh- question). When converting to direct speech, the word order must change from a statement style (*subject + verb*) to a question style (*verb + subject*). Also, the tense shifts from Past Continuous to Present Continuous.

Why the others are wrong:
(A) is wrong because it changes the "How" question into a "Yes/No" question.
(B) is wrong because it incorrectly keeps the pronoun "my" instead of changing it to "your".
(D) is wrong because it uses the statement word order (*you are*) instead of the question word order (*are you*).

questions.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech.

Joey said to the girl, “How are you doing?”
options: Joey asked the girl if she was doing fine.
Joey asked the girl how was she doing.
Joey asked the girl that how was she doing.
Joey asked the girl how she was doing.
questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is Joey asked the girl how she was doing.

Key Points

• The correct answer is option 4, "Joey asked the girl how she was doing."

• The given sentence is in direct speech, and we need to convert it into indirect speech.

• In indirect speech, we report what someone else has said without using their exact words.

• The general rule for converting direct speech to reported speech is to:

• Use a reporting verb (such as say, ask, tell) in the appropriate tense

• Change the pronouns and possessive adjectives if necessary

• Change the tense of the verb if necessary

• Change time and place expressions if necessary

• Let's apply this rule to the given sentence:

• Direct speech: Joey said to the girl, "How are you doing?"

• Reported speech: Joey asked the girl how she was doing.

• Here, the reporting verb "asked" is used in the past tense because the original statement was made in the past.

• The pronoun "you" is changed to "she" because we are reporting what Joey said to someone else.

• The question word "how" and the verb "was" are kept the same, and we use the correct word order for indirect questions.

• Thus, the correct answer is Option 4.

Correct Indirect Speech: *Joey asked the girl how she was doing. *

Additional Information

• Now, let's look at the other options and why they are incorrect:

• Joey asked the girl if she was doing fine. - This option is close to the correct answer but uses the word "fine" which is not present in the original sentence. It's important to use the exact words when converting direct speech to reported speech.

• Joey asked the girl how was she doing. - This option uses an incorrect word order. In reported speech, we use the word order of a statement, not a question.

• Joey asked the girl that how was she doing. - This option uses an incorrect word order and also adds the word "that" which is not necessary in reported speech.

• Therefore, the correct option is 4, "Joey asked the girl how she was doing."

questions.q: Which of the following states has the highest fertility rate in India according to the 2011 census?

Key Points

• According to the 2011 census in India, the state with the highest fertility rate was Bihar, with a total fertility rate of 3.4.

• Population: Bihar is the third most populous state in India with a population of 104,099,452.

• It accounts for 8.58% of India's population.

• Gender Ratio: The sex ratio in Bihar has improved marginally from 919 in 2001 to 918 in 2011.

• However, the state still has one of the lowest gender ratios in India.

• Literacy Rate: The literacy rate in Bihar has improved significantly from 47.0% in 2001 to 61.8% in 2011.

• However, it is still lower than the national average of 74.04%.

questions.q: In 1962, who published 'The History of Ocean Basins', which outlined the theory of how tectonic plates could move, later called 'sea floor spreading'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Harry Hammond Hess.

Key Points

• In 1962, Harry Hammond Hess, a geologist and Navy officer, published 'The History of Ocean Basins', which outlined the theory of how tectonic plates could move, later called 'sea floor spreading'.

• Hess proposed that new ocean crust was being continuously formed at mid-ocean ridges, where magma rises from the mantle and solidifies, pushing older crust away from the ridge and eventually causing it to subduct or be destroyed at deep-sea trenches.

• This theory, which became known as plate tectonics, revolutionized the field of geology and helped explain a wide range of geological phenomena, from the distribution of earthquakes and volcanoes to the formation of mountains and the evolution of life on Earth.

Additional Information

• Plate Tectonic Theory:

• Plate tectonic theory describes the movement of the Earth's lithosphere, which is composed of several large and many smaller plates, driven by the convective motion of the mantle.

• These plates move relative to one another, resulting in the formation of new crust at mid-ocean ridges and the destruction of old crust at subduction zones.

• This movement is responsible for a wide range of geological phenomena, including the distribution of earthquakes and volcanoes, the formation of mountain ranges, and the evolution of continents.

• For example, the collision of the Indian and Eurasian plates formed the Himalayas, and the separation of the African and South American plates created the Atlantic Ocean.

• The theory also explains the distribution of fossils, as species separated by the movement of plates evolved differently.

• Primary alcohols are those in which the carbon atom attached to the OH group is connected with one alkyl group (RCH2-OH).

• Secondary alcohols are those in which the carbon atom attached to the OH group is connected with two alkyl groups (R2CH-OH).

• Tertiary alcohols are those in which the carbon atom attached to the OH group is connected with three alkyl groups (R3C-OH).

• The general name for alcohol is 'alkyl alcohol', Ex: methyl alcohol, ethyl alcohol, etc.

• The IUPAC name of alcohols is written using the suffix 'ol' as an alkanol, Ex: methanol, ethanol, etc.

Additional Information: Acids

• Acids are the compounds containing the carboxylic (COOH)group.

• It has the general formulaR-COOH.

Phenols

• Phenols are compounds containing OH groups attached to a benzene ring.

• The general formula of phenol is C6H5-OH.

Aldehydes

• Aldehydes are the compound containing the -CHO (aldehyde) functional group.

• The general formula for aldehydes is R-CHO.

Ethers

questions.q: Which law was studied in the year 1787, in which it was said that the volume of a gas increases with its absolute temperature and if its absolute temperature decreases, then its volume will decrease?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Charles's law

Key Points:

• Avogadro's law combines the conclusions of Dalton’s atomic theory and Gay Lussac’s law of combining volumes.

• It states that equal volumes of all gases under the same conditions of temperature and pressure contain equal number of molecules.

• Mathematically it can be written as V ∝ n, where n is the number of moles of the gas.

• The number of molecules in one mole of a gas is 6.022 x 1023 and is known as the Avogadro constant.

• Gay Lussac’s Law:

• At constant volume, pressure of a fixed amount of a gas varies directly with the temperature.

• Mathematically, {p over T} = Constant = k₃.

• Charles’ Law:

• At constant pressure, the volume of a fixed mass of a gas is directly proportional to its absolute temperature.

• Mathematically, {V over T} = Constant = k₂ .

• Boyle’s Law:

• At constant temperature, the pressure of a fixed amount of gas varies inversely with its volume.

• Mathematically, p ∝ {1 over V}.

questions.q: Which among the following statements is incorrect about secondary memory?
options: It is known as the backup memory.
Data is permanently stored even if power is switched OFF.
Computer may run without the secondary memory.
questions.solution:
Correct Answer: It is a volatile memory.

• Secondary memory is also known as auxiliary memory or external memory.

• It is a type of computer memory that is used for long-term storage of data and programs, and it is not directly accessible to the CPU.

• Secondary memory is non-volatile, which means that data stored on it is not lost when the power is switched off.

• It is used for tasks such as storing operating systems, software applications, documents, media files, and other types of data that need to be accessed frequently but do not need to be kept in the primary memory (RAM) of the computer.

Additional Information

• It is known as the backup memory: This statement is correct. Secondary memory is often used as a backup for data that is stored in primary memory (RAM).

• This is because the data stored in RAM is volatile and can be lost if the power is turned off or if there is a system crash.

• By contrast, data stored in secondary memory is non-volatile and can be retrieved even if the computer shuts down unexpectedly.

• Data is permanently stored even if power is switched OFF: This statement is correct.

• As mentioned earlier, secondary memory is non-volatile, which means that it retains data even when the power is switched off.

• This is in contrast to primary memory (RAM), which is volatile and loses its contents when the power is turned off.

• Computer may run without the secondary memory: This statement is also correct.

• While secondary memory is an important component of a computer system, a computer can still run without it.

• However, the absence of secondary memory will limit the amount of data and programs that the computer can store and access.

• The computer will have to rely solely on its primary memory (RAM), which is usually much smaller in capacity than secondary memory.

questions.q: Which among the following generations of computer used the technology of transistors for the first time?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the Second generation of computers used the technology of transistors for the first time.

• The Second generation of computers (1956-1963) used transistors instead of vacuum tubes, which were used in the first generation of computers.

• Transistors were smaller, faster, and more reliable than vacuum tubes, and they consumed less power.

• The development of transistors was a major breakthrough in computer technology, as it allowed for the creation of smaller, faster, and more reliable computers.

• The second generation of computers also saw the introduction of magnetic core memory, which was faster and more reliable than the drum memory used in the first generation of computers.

Additional Information

• Third Generation: The third generation of computers (1964-1971) saw the introduction of integrated circuits, which were smaller and more reliable than transistors. Integrated circuits allowed for the creation of even smaller and faster computers, and they paved the way for the development of microprocessors.

• First Generation: The first generation of computers (1940s-1950s) used vacuum tubes as the primary electronic component. Vacuum tubes were large, fragile, and consumed a lot of power, and they were prone to failure. The first generation of computers were huge, expensive, and used mainly for scientific and military applications.

• Fourth Generation: The fourth generation of computers (1971-1989) saw the introduction of microprocessors, which were integrated circuits that contained all the components of a computer's central processing unit (CPU) on a single chip. Microprocessors were smaller, faster, and more energy-efficient than the previous generation of computers, and they led to the development of personal computers (PCs). The fourth generation of computers also saw the development of the graphical user interface (GUI) and the mouse, which made computers more user-friendly and accessible to non-technical users.
